# D2. Numerical checks {#num}

Section {{< var p.sec_numerical >}} of the paper computes date-specific Markov policy functions by backward induction
along the demographic transition, and tests every candidate equilibrium at each state; the technical documentation
[@BergGE26doc] gives the algorithms. The first table compares the date-specific solution with a time-invariant policy
function, the approximation of much of the quantitative politico-economic literature, at the same dates. The second
counts, for every file of results behind an exhibit, the equilibria and the candidates found at any state, and the
states at which no candidate passed the test and the solver fell back on the integral rule. A single equilibrium at
every state means that the selection rule of section {{< var p.sec_numerical >}} never had to choose.
